title: Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers

access.edition_or_version: Public-domain Greek text at ToposText (work 221), Book VI consulted at section 6.103ff; English: trans. R. D. Hicks, Loeb Classical Library, 2 vols. (1925)

mechanics.premise: A compilation of the lives, sayings, and doctrines of the philosophers of Greece; Book VI transmits the Cynics, above all Diogenes of Sinope.
mechanics.point_of_view: Doxographic compiler reporting sayings and anecdotes from earlier sources without sustained critical evaluation; the reader receives acts and quips, not commentary on them.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Anecdote and chreia (saying) as the unit of philosophy; biographical sequence; juxtaposition of doctrine with conduct; the stance shown through what the philosopher does in public.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Reported life -> escalating provocation -> the stance hardened into legend; the reader's discomfort is the point of the anecdotes.
mechanics.conventions: The foremost surviving source for ancient Greek philosophy; the textual vehicle through which the Cynic school reached the modern world.
tone_mechanisms: conduct rather than commentary as the unit of critique
anecdote that deflates social dignity by situation
mechanics.critical_reception: Ancient compilation whose reliability is debated (it repeats sources without consistent evaluation) yet remains primary because so much else is lost.
mechanics.verification_note: Work identity and status as the foremost surviving source confirmed via Wikipedia API extract (Diogenes Laertius) on 2026-09-24; Book VI locator (ToposText section 6.103) consulted; Hicks Loeb edition identified from catalog metadata. Analysis is partial: lineage claims rest on Book VI's transmission of Cynic practice, not on a full reading; no passage reproduced.
